title: Feige's small-deviation conjecture
formal:
For every positive integer n and independent nonnegative real random variables \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\) with \(\mathbb E X_i\le1\), is
\[\mathbb P\!\left[\sum_{i=1}^n X_i<\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbb E X_i+1\right]\ge e^{-1}?\]
definitions: Variables are defined on an arbitrary probability space and may have discrete, continuous or mixed distributions. Nonnegative means almost surely at least zero. Their expectations are finite by the hypotheses; independence is joint independence. The symbol e denotes the base of the natural logarithm. The inequality inside the probability is strict. No bound on the values or variances is assumed.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof or refutation of the stated proposition, with all its quantifiers and hypotheses. Verification of finitely many parameter values does not establish the universal assertion.
why: A sharp probability bound for sums with minimal hypotheses, arising in randomized algorithms and probabilistic combinatorics.

context_blocks.text: Earlier work proves the conjecture for discrete log-concave distributions, a restricted family rather than arbitrary independent variables.

Fu and coauthors announce a sharp finite-n bound in July 2026 which implies the displayed inequality. The card remains a candidate under the 2026 cutoff; this pass checks the announced statement rather than certifying its proof.
